repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#Up_Light).light_currentBrightness > 0)
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Up_Light).light_currentBrightness > 0)
(#Down_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait on Up_Light before calling Down_Light. The candidate polls the condition at the start of the body (line 2), but the input history (F1) shows Up_Light brightness was 0 at t=0 and rose to 0.1 at t=100ms. Because the candidate's `if` guard is evaluated only at t=0, it misses the rising edge that occurs at t=100ms, resulting in no action (F2). The fix implements the standard rising-edge state machine: block until the condition becomes true, then execute the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a blocking `wait until` for the rising edge, followed by the action and state update. This ensures the action fires exactly when the brightness transitions from false to true, matching the IR's `wait(..., edge rising)` semantics.
